correctness.rationale: The cycle vertex list follows both from the published half-integral vertex criterion and from an independent active-constraint argument. For a stable-set incidence vector of size k, the squared distance to a symmetric center s1 is exactly ns^2+k(1-2s). For even cycles this minimax is uniquely optimized at s=1/2 and the two complementary alternating stable sets give a sharp diameter certificate. For odd cycles the stable-vertex minimax is uniquely optimized at s=(n-1)/(2n); the n maximum stable sets average to that center, giving a global squared-distance certificate. The unique fractional vertex has squared distance 1/(4n), strictly below the claimed radius.

value.rationale: The fractional stable-set polytope is the canonical LP relaxation of a central combinatorial optimization problem, and cycles are the basic family where bipartite integrality fails in the smallest possible way. The theorem turns that integrality parity into an exact Euclidean phase transition: all vertices support the sphere in even order, whereas in odd order the unique half-integral obstruction moves near the center and only maximum stable sets support the sphere. The complete radial-shell formula supplies a family-wide structural invariant rather than a one-off numerical computation.
